gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Club Car's own spec sheet gives a range for the lithium Onward after four years (18–30 mi for the 4.0 kWh HP pack, 30–50 mi for the 7.0 kWh Extended Range pack) against 5–15 mi for the lead-acid Onward, or that the makers' motor figures only compare when both are continuous ratings (Onward lithium 3.5 kW vs E-Z-GO Freedom RXV ELiTE 3.3 kW), while the 11.7 hp / 8.7 kW on E-Z-GO's Liberty page has no rated-or-peak label.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited rival pages. The clubcar.com golf-carts page has prices and the words 'Lithium-Ion' and 'maintenance-free', but no kWh, no range, no motor rating and no warranty term. The T&T Golf Carts inventory page showed only filter controls, with no cart titles, prices or battery specs. Among the uncited top results, the clubcar.com/en/lithium-ion page gives the controller amps (375 A) and the IP67 case, but no kWh, range or warranty numbers. The Advantage Golf Cars Liberty ELiTE 4.2 listing gives price and warranty years only. ChatGPT's own answer used generic figures ('30–60 miles', '2,000–4,000+ cycles', '5–8 years') with no source. The Onward /specifications subpage, which holds the year-1 and year-4 range figures and the rated vs peak motor split, was not among the results.
decides: It confirms lithium over lead-acid in numbers from one maker's own sheet: the same Onward drops to 5–15 mi of range after four years on lead-acid but keeps 18–30 mi on the base lithium pack. It also turns the 'which lithium Onward' question into a capacity choice: 4.0 kWh vs 7.0 kWh, with the larger pack giving about 30–50 mi after four years. It stops a shopper from reading E-Z-GO Liberty's 11.7 hp as 2.5× the Onward's 4.7 hp. On continuous ratings, the Onward lithium (3.5 kW) and the Freedom RXV ELiTE (3.3 kW) are close. Battery warranty terms differ in kind as well as length. E-Z-GO's current personal page says 8 years with no amp-hour limit stated, while its fleet page says 5 years with unlimited amp-hours. Club Car's 6-year figure comes from a 2019 press release.

findings.note: Club Car states capacity in kWh. Voltage and Ah are not listed for the lithium pack. The charger is the 48 V E.R.I.C.

findings.product: Club Car Onward 4 Passenger HP Li-Ion
findings.label: Range, first year vs after four years
findings.value: Non-lifted: 20–35 mi in year 1, 18–30 mi after 4 years (HP). Extended Range: 35–55 mi in year 1, 30–50 mi after 4 years. Lifted: HP 20–35 → 18–30 mi; Extended Range 30–55 → 25–50 mi
findings.note: Club Car is the only maker found that gives aged-battery range. The non-lifted HP pack keeps about 86–90% of its year-1 range at year 4 (18/20 low end, 30/35 high end).

findings.label: Range, first year vs after four years
findings.value: Non-lifted: 20–40 mi in year 1, 5–15 mi after 4 years. Lifted: 20–35 mi → 5–10 mi
findings.note: Same spec page, six 8 V lead-acid batteries. In year 1 the lead-acid range (20–40 mi) matches or beats the lithium HP pack (20–35 mi). By year 4 it falls to 5–15 mi, against 18–30 mi for lithium. This is the footnote for the comparison table.

findings.product: Club Car Onward 4 Passenger HP Li-Ion
findings.label: Motor power, rated vs peak
findings.value: Lithium: 4.7 hp (3.5 kW) rated, 375 A controller, peak not listed. Lead-acid: 3.3 hp (2.4 kW) rated, 13 hp (9.6 kW) peak, 250 A controller
findings.note: Club Car's lead-acid line shows that peak can be about 4× rated (13 / 3.3 hp). A motor figure with no label cannot be set against a rated one.

findings.note: E-Z-GO labels this figure 'Continuous', so it compares directly with Club Car's 3.5 kW rated: the RXV ELiTE is 0.2 kW lower. E-Z-GO gives no kWh or Ah. The 'Range' field holds a speed tolerance (±0.5 mph), not a distance.

findings.label: Motor power and pack
findings.value: 11.7 hp (8.7 kW), no rated or peak label; 235 A AC controller; battery 'ELiTE 2.2, Single 56.7V Max Lithium'; 48 VDC system; range listed as 'N/A'
findings.note: Because there is no continuous/peak label, this figure is not comparable with Club Car's 4.7 hp rated or the RXV's 4.4 hp continuous. Do not rank it as more powerful. '56.7 V Max' is the maximum charge voltage; the system is 48 V nominal.
